newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-DAVIS TRIUMPH ECLIPSES WOMAN STREAKER.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-DAVIS TRIUMPH ECLIPSES WOMAN STREAKER.

text.p: Not even a woman streaker was able to overshadow a remarkable performance by snooker veteran Steve Davis at the weekend as he revived a career many thought was ending by winning the Benson and Hedges Masters.

Davis, who won the last of his six world titles in 1989 and started this tournament as a 28-1 outsider, recovered from a seemingly hopeless 8-4 down to win 10-8 against brilliant youngster Ronnie O'Sullivan.
The 22-year-old O'Sullivan began as if he intended winning in record time, racing to a 2-0 lead without Davis scoring a single point.

The appearance of the naked young woman, who jumped out of the audience and streaked around the table, may have had something to do with Davis's recovery as O'Sullivan missed a straightforward red when play resumed.
"She definitely broke Ronnie's concentration," said Davis with a smile afterwards.
Davis went on to win the third frame and later levelled at 4-4 but there were no naked women anywhere around to witness the later drama.

O'Sullivan raced through the next four frames in just 49 minutes to take an apparent stranglehold on the final. Davis, whose last title win was the Welsh Open two years ago, was probably the only one in the hall who thought differently.
With some excellent potting and superb defensive play Davis clawed his way back into contention, aided to a degree by carelessness which crept into O'Sullivan's game for the next two frames.
By the time the young Londoner regained his concentration, Davis was playing in the fashion of his earlier years when he dominated play through the 1980s.

O'Sullivan failed to win another frame, and Davis compounded his woes in frame 15 with a 130 break to snatch away from his opponent the 15,000 pounds ($24,400) for the highest break of the tournament.
Even Davis admitted afterwards to being uncertain how he had managed such an astonishing recovery. "It's all a bit of a blur," he said. "I'm not quite sure how I did it."

Davis, who slipped from second down to 10th in the world rankings last year, won 135,000 pounds ($221,000), his largest single payday in a career in which he has won over 4.5 million pounds ($6.1 million).
